doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Greensboro bebop friends and playing a regular show first
summary: Carl Foster and Billy Tolles shared his interest; they played a regular show then bebop at the end.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Now, I’m unclear from our conversation yesterday whether this was a solitary activity or whether you had people in Greensboro who were similarly interested in bebop and the new music.
Yeah, of course. Everybody in Greensboro was interested in it. My good friend, Carl Foster. This other guy I told you about, Billy Tolles, who was a great saxophonist.
Billy Tolles was from Seattle, right?
Seattle, Washington. He was a great saxophone player. He could play all that kind of stuff when he came down to North Carolina.
Now, the people you played with in Greensboro... Were you moonlighting outside of school? Did you ever do three-four days out on the road with a blues singer, or go to a dance...
No, we played in clubs. And we played bebop. We played a regular show, then we’d play bebop. You had to play a regular show first. Then we’d play some bebop tunes.
You mean at the end of the show.
At the end of the show.
Now, you said that’s been your m.o. ever since.
You play during the regular show things that will communicate to the average man and woman, and then you...
